Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani
 Order

By way of the present petition filed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, the petitioners, who are the father- in-law and mother-in-law of the complainant/respondent No. 2 seek quashing of case FIR No. 14/2022 dated 18.04.2022 registered at P.S.:
South Avenue in which, chargesheet has been filed for offences under sections 354A/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code 1860 ('IPC').
2.

Mr. Ravindra Narayan, learned counsel for the petitioners points-out that though the FIR was registered against the father-in-law, the mother-in-law as well as the sister-in-law; the chargesheet was filed only against the father-in-law and mother-in-law; while the sister-in- law was placed in column No. 12, which is why she is not party to the present petition.
3. The petition is premised on Settlement Deed dated 20.05.2022 arrived at through mediation before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi between the concerned parties.

4. The petition is supported by affidavits of both the petitioners, as also of respondent No. 2,
alongwith proofs of their I.Ds.
5. Both petitioners as well as respondent No. 2 are present in-person.
Their credentials have been verified and they have also been identified by their respective counsel.

sentences.text: Ms. Meenakshi Dahiya, learned APP confirms that the State has no objection to the subject FIR being quashed.

7. In the circumstances, in line with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported as (2012) 10 SCC 303 as also in Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported as (2014) 6 SCC 466 this court sees no reason why the subject FIR and all proceedings emanating therefrom should not be quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This court is of the view that in light of the settlement between the contesting parties, continuing with the subject FIR and all subsequent proceedings would be an exercise in futility and would not be conducive to peace and harmony between the parties.
8. Accordingly, FIR No. 14/2022 dated 18.04.2022 is quashed.
All proceedings arising therefrom also stand closed.
9. Petition stands disposed of.
10. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
